skills.name: Policy Boundary Enforcement Under Social Pressure
skills.description: Maintain correct refusal of actions that violate policy even when the user applies emotional pressure, claims special circumstances, asserts prior approval, or insists repeatedly. The agent must distinguish between legitimate edge cases and manipulation, and must not capitulate to frustration, grief, urgency, or persistence when the policy is unambiguous.
skills.reasoning: A26 (agent refunded a non-refundable cancellation), A31 (agent changed a basic economy flight it should not have), A36 (agent changed a basic economy flight despite bereavement story), A43 (agent cancelled flights that did not meet criteria when user insisted), A47 (agent cancelled without valid insurance reason), A49 (agent cancelled when user lied about having insurance), A9 (agent made concessions to flattery), R10 (returned items to wrong payment method after user insisted), R12 (transferred instead of holding the line on refund method), R47 (transferred instead of explaining refund timeline). The pattern: user escalates emotionally or socially, agent abandons correct policy behavior.

skills.name: Precise Numeric and Identifier Argument Construction
skills.description: When calling action tools, compute exact numeric parameters (amounts, counts, prices, differences) and select exact identifiers (certificate IDs, payment IDs, flight numbers, item IDs) that match the task requirements. Errors include using wrong certificate amounts, applying the wrong payment method, computing incorrect price differences, booking wrong passenger counts, or referencing wrong item IDs.
skills.reasoning: A2 (sent $300 certificate instead of $50), A8 (booked with wrong passenger or baggage details), A20 (payment amounts didn't add up), A24 (booked wrong flight variant), A25 (wrong payment split), A27 (sent $150 instead of $50 per correct passenger count), A38 (sent $150 cert instead of checking actual passenger count then $50), R1 (exchange used wrong item IDs), R23 (wrong item IDs passed to modify call), R28 (returned wrong set of items), R44 (calculated price difference incorrectly), R49 (exchanged for wrong item variant). The agent selects the right action type but constructs wrong numeric or identifier arguments.

skills.name: Multi-Constraint Option Selection
skills.description: When searching for or selecting an option (flight, product, variant) that must simultaneously satisfy multiple constraints — such as time window, price range, airport, availability, material, size, and feature requirements — correctly identify the unique option that satisfies all constraints rather than partially matching or defaulting to the most salient constraint.
skills.reasoning: A15/A16 (found multiple airports but picked wrong cheapest flight — HAT227+HAT139 instead of HAT110+HAT172), A21 (selected wrong return flight combination — needed fastest on specific date), A33 (searched wrong date for return flight), A37 (searched wrong legs when finding upgrade candidate), A14/A23 (complex multi-leg booking with specific flight numbers required), R19 (tried to exchange a non-delivered order), R60 (failed to find speaker under $100 matching constraints), R97 (address update for wrong order). Agent satisfies some constraints but misses others when they must all hold simultaneously.

skills.name: Cross-Operation State Tracking
skills.description: After performing one operation that changes an order or reservation's state (cancel, exchange request, modify), correctly track the resulting state before attempting subsequent operations on the same object. Failures include trying to exchange an item in an order that just had a return initiated, trying to modify a just-cancelled order, attempting a second exchange on an order now in 'exchange requested' status, or applying baggage updates after a flight change that changed the free-bag entitlement.
skills.reasoning: A17 (updated cabin and passenger but baggage update used wrong free-bag calculation post-cabin change), A22 (multiple modifications where one failed silently and later operations assumed earlier state), A29/A30 (baggage updates failed because flight change altered applicable rules), A39 (cancelled some reservations with refund but the tool does not allow zero-refund cancels — should have stopped earlier), R27 (returned items, then tried to exchange from same order which now had 'return requested' status), R76 (tried to remove an item by modifying with same ID, triggering 'new item same as old' error), R99 (exchanged bicycle successfully but then could not exchange puzzle from the same order now in exchange-requested state). Agent proceeds as if prior operations did not change the object's state.

skills.name: User Claim Verification and Correction
skills.description: When a user states a fact that can be verified against retrieved data — such as the number of passengers on a reservation, which payment method was used, which reservation was delayed, whether insurance was purchased, or which item was ordered — verify the claim against the actual data and gently correct the user when they are wrong, rather than accepting the user's version and acting on it.
skills.reasoning: A2 (user said 3 passengers but reservation had 2 — agent accepted 3 and issued $300 instead of $50), A38 (same scenario — user insisted 3 passengers, agent accepted without checking), A9 (user repeatedly called agent 'most lenient ever' trying to get concessions, agent kept complying emotionally), R82 (user insisted refund should go to credit card, but original payment was gift card — agent eventually processed to gift card but only after confusion), R83 (same scenario, agent correctly identified gift card but still escalated), R80 (user could not decide about exchange — agent kept engaging with the emotional conversation instead of focusing on the task), R67 (user could not recall zip code and kept guessing — agent failed to guide user to correct identification). The skill: distinguish what the user claims from what the data shows, verify before acting.

skills.name: Task Completion vs. Partial-Action Termination
skills.description: Complete all components of a multi-part task before ending the conversation, and avoid terminating or 'resolving' the task after completing only a subset of the required actions. Conversely, do not take actions beyond what was requested. Failures include completing only the first of several required changes, issuing unsolicited certificates or compensation, or failing to book the additional new reservation after cancelling the old one.
skills.reasoning: A7 (cancelled one reservation but not both, and failed to upgrade first as required), A11 (downgraded correctly but did not explicitly refuse passenger removal — just silently skipped it), A18 (downgraded first reservation then stopped, missing 4 others), A39 (cancelled some but not the correct set of reservations), A41 (did not check all 7 reservations — stopped after 1), A42 (ended conversation after checking reservations without identifying and cancelling the correct duplicates), A44 (cancelled one reservation but failed to perform the upgrades), R33 (cancelled entire order instead of selective cancellation), R34 (cancelled entire order instead of selective removal), R65 (tried to modify a processed order instead of placing the new separate order). The agent resolves the conversation prematurely or incompletely.
